name: JSON Formatter
description: Format, validate, and minify JSON with clear, line-and-column error messages — all in your browser.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: No. Parsing and formatting use the browser's built-in JSON.parse and JSON.stringify — your data never leaves your device, which matters if you're pasting real API responses or config with sensitive values.

faq.question: Why does it say my JSON is invalid when it looks fine?
faq.answer: Common causes are trailing commas, single quotes instead of double quotes, or unquoted object keys — none of which are valid in strict JSON even though they're valid in JavaScript object literals. The error message includes the line and column where parsing failed.

faq.question: What does 'minify' do?
faq.answer: It re-serializes your JSON with no extra whitespace, producing the smallest valid representation of the same data — useful for shipping config or API payloads.
